_comment: Settings for the binder builder. This file IS one binder definition - it declares what that binder contains. Every binder_builder_settings*.json in this folder is a binder, and one run builds them all. Any key starting with _comment is ignored by the tool - JSON has no comment syntax, so notes live in keys like this one.
_comment_name: The binder's name. Used in the heading ("<name> Binder") and in the filename ("<name>_Binder_v<number>.md"). It also identifies this binder on the command line, and no two definitions in one folder may share it.
name: AIDE_Documentation
_comment_root: The folder the binder is built from, including everything beneath it unless subfolders is false. A relative path is resolved against the folder this script lives in, so ".." means the parent folder.
_comment_subfolders: true walks the whole tree from root. false collects from root only.
_comment_paths: include and exclude accept three kinds of path. ABSOLUTE - "C:/Docs/_binder" - names one exact folder. ROOT-ANCHORED - "~/_binder" - names one exact folder, measured from the root above. RELATIVE - "_binder" - is a pattern rather than a place: it matches every folder in the tree whose path ends with those segments, so one entry covers a _binder subfolder wherever it appears. Note that ~ means the root of the tree here, never your home folder.
_comment_defaults: The tool skips two kinds of folder by default, without any entry in exclude. (1) Any folder whose name starts with an underscore. (2) The asset folders: assets, images, img and media. Use include to override a default skip for a specific folder. include does not include a default-skipped folder's own default-skipped children, so including _rebuild does not include _rebuild/_superseded.
_comment_include: Folders skipped by default that should be collected from anyway. See _comment_defaults above for what is skipped and why. ~/_rebuild is a leftover from the temporary arrangement described below and no longer earns its place - see _comment_exclude_files_outstanding.
_comment_exclude: Folders to skip entirely, along with everything inside them. Exclude always wins over include. Infrastructure is machinery that acts on the corpus and is never loaded into an AI session, so it is excluded from the binder it builds.
_comment_file_types: File extensions to collect, without the dot. json is here so that data and configuration documents are carried. Note that nothing currently excludes JSON: the _tools and _config folders are underscore-prefixed and so out of scope anyway, and Infrastructure is excluded, but JSON dropped into _rebuild WOULD be collected. Add "~/_rebuild/*.json" to exclude_files if that becomes a problem.
_comment_exclude_files: Files to skip. Applied AFTER file_types has chosen what to collect, so this setting only ever removes, and it is the last word. Three forms, the same convention include and exclude use for folders. FILENAME - "*_WIP_*" - matched against the name wherever the file appears. ROOT-ANCHORED - "~/_rebuild/*.json" - one exact path, measured from the root. TRAILING - "_rebuild/*.json" - a pattern rather than a place: any file whose path ends with those segments.
_comment_exclude_files_wildcards: ? matches one character. In the two path forms * stops at a folder separator and ** crosses them: "~/_rebuild/*.json" is JSON directly in _rebuild, while "~/_rebuild/**/*.json" is JSON in _rebuild and everything beneath it. The filename form has no separators to stop at.
_comment_exclude_files_rule: THE RULE - THE TEST IS DURABILITY, NOT CADENCE. The working document holds what is current-and-transient, plus pending content destined for masters not yet written; it is excluded and loaded separately when it is needed. Everything that outlives the session is binder-class and belongs IN the binder - work registers and open-items documents both. Cadence is not the test: registers and open items churn at session cadence in raw terms, and the discipline that makes them binder-safe is writing at master update, which any document can adopt. What cannot be made binder-safe is content that is meaningless outside the session that produced it. Never add an exclusion for a register or an open-items document here.
_comment_exclude_files_standing: THE STANDING EXCLUSIONS are "*_WIP_*" and "*_WIP.*", and they are IN FORCE. The second is a wide catch for a WIP file carrying no version suffix, which should not happen but might. The temporary lifting of these two, which ran from 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-08 while the binder would otherwise have been empty, has ended: the binder now records an empty scope rather than carrying the working document to avoid one.
_comment_exclude_files_outstanding: ONE HALF OF THE OLD TRIGGER IS STILL OUTSTANDING. The arrangement had two parts: restore the *_WIP_* exclusions, and remove ~/_rebuild from include. Only the first has been done. ~/_rebuild is therefore still walked, and everything in it is currently excluded only because every document in it is a WIP file - a non-WIP document dropped into _rebuild WOULD enter the binder. Remove ~/_rebuild from include when Project Design masters land, or sooner if that surprises anyone.
_comment_order: Optional. Filenames pulled to the front of the binder, in the order listed. A name that matches nothing in scope is reported, not silently ignored.
_comment_output: The folder the binder is written to. The default "~/_binder" is an underscore folder inside the root, so it is skipped by the walk and a binder can never contain itself.
_comment_log_file: Where the run log is appended. One entry per run, never overwritten. Named for this binder, so several definitions in one folder do not interleave their runs in one file. Leave the setting out entirely and the tool derives exactly this name.
